definitions.type: family of Euclidean metric spaces indexed by natural numbers, together with their coordinate notation
definitions.definition: For each natural k, V(k)=ℝ^k, the functions from {0,...,k-1} to ℝ, with distance d(x,y)=(Σ_{j=0}^{k-1}(x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2) and its metric topology and Borel measurable structure. V(0) consists of the single empty tuple. ℝ has its usual absolute-value distance. V(k)×ℝ always means the metric with squared distance d(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2, not the max-product metric. Concatenation (x,t)↦(x_0,...,x_{k-1},t) specifies the identification with V(k+1).

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X and A⊆X, diam(A)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈A,y∈A} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set equal to 0. On a metric space edist is ordinary distance viewed in [0,∞]. This is the native Metric.ediam. When diam(A) is bounded by a finite scale we identify it with its finite nonnegative real value. In particular empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: positive-exponent unnormalized Hausdorff contents and measure, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of that Euclidean space

definitions.type: native Hausdorff measures on Borel extended metric spaces, indexed by real exponents
definitions.definition: μH[d] on a Borel extended metric space X denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d, defined natively as Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^d), the metric outer-measure construction with diameter gauge r^d followed by its Borel measure. The metric outer construction is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the infimum of Σ_i (sup_{h:U_i≠∅} diam(U_i)^d) over sequences U:ℕ→Set X covering the set and satisfying diam(U_i)≤r. Empty summands are zero, including at exponent zero. Native ENNReal real powers are used. The value formula for the resulting measure on arbitrary subsets is established by the registered native theorem; its identification with H for positive exponents is proved below.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of a metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric space with its Borel structure, dim_H(A)=sup{u:u∈[0,∞) is finite and μH[u](A)=∞}, with supremum of the empty set zero. The metric space may be borelized when no measurable structure was specified. This is the native dimH definition. Thus dim_H(∅)=0 by this convention. In this task it is applied to Euclidean subsets and the Euclidean product metric of V(n)×ℝ.

definitions.type: subset of V(n)×ℝ with the Euclidean product metric
definitions.definition: F=E×I={(x,t):x∈E,t∈I}, using the squared-distance product metric specified in V. Its Euclidean identification is the concatenation map to V(n+1).
D=dim_H(E). When finiteness is proved, finite dimensions are also viewed as nonnegative real numbers through the canonical inclusion ℝ≥0→[0,∞].

inputs.statement: For every Euclidean subset A and s>0, the supplied unnormalized H^s(A) equals native μH[s](A). The native dim_H therefore has the following critical-exponent properties with this H: s>dim_H(A) implies H^s(A)=0; 0<s<dim_H(A) implies H^s(A)=∞; H^s(A)=0 implies dim_H(A)≤s; H^s(A)=∞ implies dim_H(A)≥s. Always dim_H(A)≥0. For 0<δ≤r, H^s_δ(A)≥H^s_r(A), and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0}H^s_δ(A); if H^s(A)=∞ these contents are unbounded as δ↓0. If A⊆B in one Euclidean space, then dim_H(A)≤dim_H(B). If φ:A→Y is distance preserving into another Euclidean space Y, then H^s(φ(A))=H^s(A) for every s>0 and dim_H(φ(A))=dim_H(A), with both sets given their ambient Euclidean metrics. For every a>0, h^a→0 as h↓0; for every b<0, h^b→∞ as h↓0. Nonnegative series are sums in [0,∞], i.e. suprema of finite partial sums; Σ_{i≥0}2^{-i-1}=1 and Σ_{i≥0}2^{-i-2}=1/2.

binders.type: subset of the same Euclidean space

inputs.statement: 0≤D≤n, in particular D is finite and may be viewed as a nonnegative real. E is bounded. For every s>0 and δ>0, H^s_δ(E)<∞. If n=0, E=V(0), a singleton, and D=0. The concatenation map V(n)×ℝ→V(n+1) of D001 is a bijective isometry, so the product metric used for F is exactly the Euclidean metric required in the target.

output.statement: If n≥1, then for every real q>D, every 0<r≤1 and every ε>0 there exist a countable index set K and nonempty sets U_i⊆V(n) (i∈K) covering E such that, writing r_i=diam(U_i), 0<r_i≤r and Σ_{i∈K}r_i^q<ε.

binders.type: family of finite real diameters of U

locals.declaration: Choose the scale-r cover W with cost <ε/2 supplied by F001.

locals.type: subset of ℕ used as a countable index type

locals.declaration: For i∈K leave W_i fixed if its diameter is positive. If it is a singleton, let U_i be the closed ball centered at its unique point, of diameter min(r/2,(ε2^{-i-3})^{1/q}); n≥1 ensures that ball has exactly this positive diameter.

argument.text: Assume L1: n≥1, q>D, 0<r≤1 and ε>0, with q,r,ε arbitrary. N002 gives D≥0, hence q>0. N001 gives H^q(E)=0 and therefore H^q_r(E)=0. By the defining infimum of H^q_r, there is a countable scale-r cover of E of q-cost <ε/2: if all admissible costs were at least ε/2 their infimum would be at least ε/2. Countable covers may be enumerated by ℕ and padded with empty members.

produces.statement: There exists W:ℕ→Set V(n) covering E with diam(W_i)≤r for every i and Σ_i diam(W_i)^q<ε/2, where empty-member cost is zero; moreover q>0.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Discard empty members and let K={i:W_i≠∅}. A nonempty zero-diameter W_i is a singleton, since distance zero identifies any two of its points. For each such i take the positive number min(r/2,(ε2^{-i-3})^{1/q}) and replace W_i by the closed ball centered at its unique point, with radius half that number. It has positive diameter at most r and q-cost ≤ε2^{-i-3}<ε2^{-i-2}; the power identity is valid because q>0. The diameter is exactly the prescribed number because n≥1: two opposite points in the first-coordinate direction belong to the closed ball, and the triangle inequality supplies the reverse diameter bound. Leave every positive-diameter member unchanged. Define U_i to be this resulting family on K and r_i=diam(U_i). The cover still contains every W_i and hence covers E, with 0<r_i≤r. Its total q-cost is at most the original cost plus Σ_{i≥0}ε2^{-i-2}≤ original cost+ε/2<ε, using the geometric sum in N001 and finite-partial-sum comparisons. This is the supplied replacement argument with an explicit permissible choice of the small diameters. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q,r,ε.
